![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14059223/assets/85aff149fcbad4437f64f7d6eab96a42a287417c6c8f5483a03bf6fc2f22b930.png)

The graph of the function $y=g(x)$ is shown above. Approximate ${g}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=4$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{g}^{′}(x)≈\frac{g(x+h)-g(x-h)}{2h},
$$

at the point $x=4$ with step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(4) & ≈\frac{g(4+1)-g(4-1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{g(5)-g(3)}{2} \\  & =\frac{4-2}{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
